summary: The main article describes a visible-light photocatalytic strategy for N-radical cascade reactions of hydrazones, featuring 1 table for optimization, 9 figures/schemes detailing reaction design, computational profiles, and substrate scopes. The work includes mechanistic investigations and synthetic applications for producing 1,6-dihydropyradazines and diazinium salts.

items.heading: Figure 1
items.caption: Reaction design. ( a ) Visible-light-induced photocatalytic generation of N-centred radicals from N-functionalized precursors. ( b ) Our blueprint for catalytic N-radical cascade reaction of hydrazones: merge of oxidative deprotonation electron transfer (ODET) activation of N-H bond with TEMPO mediation.
items.description: This figure illustrates the general concept of photocatalytic N-radical generation and the specific ODET/TEMPO-mediation strategy proposed by the authors.

items.heading: Figure 2
items.caption: Reaction development. ( a ) Generation of N-radicals by visible-light photocatalysis. ( b ) Free energy profiles for 5exo and 6endo radical cyclizations of 1a-A . ( c ) Free energy profiles for 5exo and 6endo radical cyclizations of 1b-A . ( d ) Free energy profiles for 5exo and 6endo radical cyclizations of 1c-A .
items.description: This figure presents DFT-calculated free energy profiles comparing 5-exo and 6-endo radical cyclization pathways for different hydrazone substrates.

items.heading: Figure 3
items.caption: Initial results. ( a ) Reaction of substrate 1a and 1b under condition A . ( b ) Reaction of substrate 1c under condition A .
items.description: This figure shows the experimental outcomes for initial substrates, demonstrating the regioselectivity observed in 5-exo versus 6-endo cyclizations.

items.heading: Table 1
items.caption: Optimization of reaction conditions .
items.description: This table summarizes the screening of photocatalysts, bases, solvents, and additives to optimize the yield of 1,6-dihydropyridazine 2c.

items.heading: Figure 4
items.caption: Reaction scope of unsaturated hydrazones. ( a ) Investigation of the effects of arene substitution of hydrazones. ( b ) Substrate scope of aliphatic unsaturated hydrazones. ( c ) Substrate scope of alkene moieties.
items.description: This figure displays the broad substrate scope of the reaction, including various aryl, heteroaryl, and aliphatic hydrazones.

items.heading: Figure 5
items.caption: Mechanistic investigations. ( a ) Trapping the C-centred intermediate by addition of PhSeSePh or BHT under the standard conditions. ( b ) Trapping the C-centred intermediate by addition of PhSeSePh under the standard conditions in the absence of TEMPO. ( c ) Control experiment with selenide-adduct 7 under the standard conditions.
items.description: This figure details radical trapping experiments used to probe the existence of C-centered radical intermediates and the role of TEMPO.

items.heading: Figure 6
items.caption: Calculation studies. ( a ) Free energy profile for the transformation of C-centred radical 1c-C into product 2c through a TEMPO-mediated HATprocess. ( b ) Free energy profile for the transformation of C-centred radical 1c-C into product 2c through carbon radical trapping/elimination process.
items.description: Computational free energy profiles comparing the HAT process versus the radical trapping/elimination pathway for the final product formation.

items.heading: Figure 7
items.caption: Proposed catalytic cycle. The plausible mechanism involves oxidative deprotonation electron transfer (ODET) activation of N-H bond into N-centred radical by visible light photoredox catalysis and TEMPO-mediated N-radical cyclization.
items.description: A comprehensive diagram showing the proposed catalytic cycle, including the photoredox cycle and the radical cascade steps.

items.heading: Figure 8
items.caption: Synthetic application. ( a ) Gram-scale reaction. ( b ) One-pot process for synthesis of 1,6-dihydropyridazine 2d . ( c ) Synthesis of pyridazine N -oxide 14 .
items.description: This figure demonstrates the practical utility of the method through scale-up, one-pot synthesis, and further chemical transformations.

items.heading: Figure 9
items.caption: Application to the synthesis of pyridazines and diazinium salts. ( a ) Reactions were run with 2 or 6 (0.2 mmol), NaOH (0.6 mmol) and CH3CN (4.0ml) at 80 ° C for 3-5 h. ( b ) Reactions were run with 15 (0.3 mmol), 16 (0.6 mmol) and acetone (3.0 ml) at 100 ° C for 12 h.
items.description: This figure shows the conversion of dihydropyridazines into pyridazines and subsequently into diazinium salts for biological testing.
